title: Three-channel anticommutator bridge for half-density modular tails
question: Can the Gibbs half-density anticommutator and commutator costs be decomposed into left/right GNS legs and a positive beta/2 two-slice cross term, so the unresolved modular tail is separated into independently controllable channels?
promotion_boundary: R-379 is a finite exact three-channel decomposition of the R-378 half-density costs. It exposes a beta/2 two-slice term but proves no uniform bound for any channel, no common core or common alpha, and no QFT limit.
next_action: Establish a source-, volume- and cutoff-uniform estimate for the left and right GNS legs and the beta/2 two-slice leg on one Hamiltonian-derived core; then combine the channel bounds with R-378 and the R-377 resolvent telescope.
boundary: Finite actual-Q3 edge and square doubled-bond Gibbs proxies with all prefixes, translated sites, signs and adjoints on the declared cutoffs. The three-channel identities and cross envelope are checked numerically and in Lean; modular tails, source/volume/cutoff uniformity, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
